messages:
Ivy: Heads up — Crestline Data had a sustained p95 token latency bump (~240ms) during their ETL/marketing batch window 11:05-11:25 UTC. Renewal discussion in 5 days, want to propose a non-disruptive perf plan.
Marco: Do we know invocation mix? streaming vs non-streaming, and embeddings?
Ivy: Mixed workload. ~65% non-streaming chat completions (median prompt 140 tokens, median response 110), ~25% streaming assistant sessions, ~10% embeddings for semantic search. Spike aligned with parallel marketing job bursts.
Zoe: Key risk for streaming is tail latency when we backpressure. If we change quant or model we should ensure streaming time-to-first-token (TTFT) stays stable.
Ivy: Proposed multi-prong plan: 1) enable a dynamic quant routing policy: short prompts (<120 tokens) -> compact-lite:int8, long prompts -> full-v1, 2) 12% canary for compact-lite:int8, 3) hosted fallback 12% to avoid customer-visible regressions, 4) enable prefix cache for top-30 prefixes.
Marco: Nice. Dynamic routing by prompt length minimizes semantic regressions for long, sensitive prompts. We should also gate streaming sessions to avoid mixing canary outputs mid-session.
Ivy: Good point — add rule: streaming sessions pinned to baseline model for session duration. That keeps TTFT stable.
Anika (Crestline): Concern: embeddings accuracy — we rely on vector parity for search. Will int8 on compact-lite hurt embedding distances?
Zoe: Embeddings will not route to compact-lite in this plan. Keep embeddings on hosted/full-v1. Also plan to run a 20-sample embedding parity check for due diligence.
Ivy: Draft route policy snippet below:
```
route: crestline-dynamic-quant
- match: customer_id == "crestline"
- dynamic_rules:
  - if prompt_length < 120 and request_type == "completion": model=redwood/compact-lite:int8
  - if request_type == "streaming": model=redwood/full-v1
  - if request_type == "embedding": model=redwood/full-v1
- weights: {dedicated: 76, hosted_fallback: 12, canary: 12}
- canary: {model: redwood/compact-lite:int8, weight: 12, duration: 2h}
- prefix_cache_top_k: 30
- autoscale_headroom: 0.22
- continuous_batch_size_limit: 48
- rollback: {p95_delta_ms: 160, error_rate_pct: 0.5}
```
Marco: Ops notes: we should also set session_pin=true for streaming sessions and increase KV-prefetch TTL to 90s for the dedicated pool to stabilize cache hits. Pre-warm top-30 prefixes as part of canary start.
Zoe: Add semantic regression gate: run automated semantic-similarity (embedding cosine) on a 25-sample eval set for the compact-lite path, require mean cosine >= 0.985 before stepping beyond 12%. Also capture TTFT for streaming sessions and require no >5% increase.
Ivy: ops-bot, please schedule the canary and create alerts: crestline-canary-p95, crestline-canary-ttft, crestline-embedding-delta. Rollback if p95 > baseline+160ms for 10m OR ttft increase >5% OR embedding_delta_mean < 0.985.
ops-bot: Canary scheduled: crestline-dynamic-4832101111; monitors created: p95_tokens, ttft_streaming, embedding_cosine_mean; auto-revert rules set as requested.
Anika (Crestline): Thanks all. QA will run the 25-sample eval tomorrow morning and join a quick 30m call at 15:00 UTC to sign off. Please include our search lead for the embedding check.
Ivy: Great — action items: Ivy prepare eval sets, Marco implement canary route + pre-warm, Zoe run semantic & embedding checks, ops-bot run canary and alerts. We'll post interim metrics in this thread after 30m and 2h windows. :white_check_mark:
